Assert that a status only changes in allowed ways

Source: R/transitions.R
ensure_transitions.Rd

A checkpoint for a status that follows a unit over time: a person who has completed an education must not later be not started on it. Name the transitions that cannot happen, or a final status that nothing else may follow, and the rows where they happen are reported, counted per transition. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_transitions(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  status,
  forbid = NULL,
  final = NULL,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

time

The period column, or the start of a spell (one column).

status

The status column (one column).

forbid

Forbidden transitions, as strings "from -> to".

final

Statuses that, once reached, must not change.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when a forbidden transition happens and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

Each row is compared with the unit's next observation in time, whatever the distance, as in describe_transitions(), which shows every transition there is before you write the rule. Rows with a missing time or status are left out. The unit is what the id columns say: give id = c(cpr, education) when a person may complete one education and start another.

The rule is given as forbidden pairs, forbid = "completed -> enrolled", since few statuses only go forward in a fixed order: an interrupted education can be resumed, a completed one cannot. A final status, final = "completed", is the common case written short: every change away from it is forbidden. Statuses are compared as text, so a numeric status is written as its number, "3 -> 1".

On failure the reported rows are the rows the forbidden transition goes to, with a transition column naming it and a previous column holding the time of the observation it comes from.

See also

describe_transitions() to see every transition first, carry_status() to let a final status stand, checkpoints.

Examples

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"),
  year   = c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2019, 2020, 2019, 2021),
  status = c("not started", "enrolled", "completed",
             "enrolled", "completed", "completed", "not started")
)
ensure_transitions(education, cpr, year, status, final = "completed")
#> Warning: Forbidden transitions: status by year per cpr
#> ℹ 1 row in 1 group
#>   In 1 unit
#>   By transition: completed -> not started (1)
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     transition               cpr   previous  year status
#>     <chr>                    <chr>    <dbl> <dbl> <chr>
#>   1 completed -> not started c         2019  2021 not started
#> ℹ If the final status is right and the later ones wrong: carry_status(education, cpr, year, status, final = "completed")

ensure_transitions(education, cpr, year, status,
                   forbid = c("completed -> not started", "enrolled -> not started"))
#> Warning: Forbidden transitions: status by year per cpr
#> ℹ 1 row in 1 group
#>   In 1 unit
#>   By transition: completed -> not started (1)
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     transition               cpr   previous  year status
#>     <chr>                    <chr>    <dbl> <dbl> <chr>
#>   1 completed -> not started c         2019  2021 not started
